You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE continents (
    ContId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Continent TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE countries (
    CountryId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    CountryName TEXT,
    Continent INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Continent) REFERENCES continents(ContId)
);

CREATE TABLE car_makers (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker TEXT,
    FullName TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Country) REFERENCES countries(CountryId)
);

CREATE TABLE model_list (
    ModelId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Maker INTEGER,
    Model TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Model),
    FOREIGN KEY (Maker) REFERENCES car_makers(Id)
);

CREATE TABLE car_names (
    MakeId INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    Model TEXT,
    Make TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (Model) REFERENCES model_list(Model)
);

CREATE TABLE cars_data (
    Id INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    MPG TEXT,
    Cylinders INTEGER,
    Edispl REAL,
    Horsepower TEXT,
    Weight INTEGER,
    Accelerate REAL,
    Year INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (Id) REFERENCES car_names(MakeId)
);

What kind of “old car makers” analysis do you want—oldest *makers by first model year in this dataset*, or *cars from older years by maker*?

Here are a few useful queries (pick one and I can tailor it):

### 1) Oldest year each maker appears in the data (and how many cars they have)
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year_in_data,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year_in_data,
  COUNT(*) AS cars_in_data
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml   ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn    ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd    ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year_in_data ASC, cars_in_data DESC;
```

### 2) “Oldest makers” (top N by earliest year)
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year_in_data
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year_in_data ASC
LIMIT 10;
```

### 3) Makers with the most cars before a cutoff year (e.g., <= 1975)
```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  COUNT(*) AS cars_up_to_1975
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data cd  ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
WHERE cd.Year <= 1975
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY cars_up_to_1975 DESC;
```

### 4) Oldest cars (rows) with maker + model
```sql
SELECT
  cd.Year,
  cm.Maker,
  cn.Model,
  cd.MPG, cd.Cylinders, cd.Edispl, cd.Horsepower, cd.Weight
FROM cars_data cd
JOIN car_names cn  ON cn.MakeId = cd.Id
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Model = cn.Model
JOIN car_makers cm ON cm.Id = ml.Maker
ORDER BY cd.Year ASC
LIMIT 25;
```

Tell me:
1) What do you mean by “old” (earliest year? before 1970/1975?), and  
2) Do you want results by maker only, or maker + model?
focus on makers that produced vehicles a long time ago

```sql
-- Makers that produced vehicles a long time ago (earliest appearance in dataset),
-- plus how long they span in the data.
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
  (MAX(cd.Year) - MIN(cd.Year)) AS span_years,
  COUNT(*) AS vehicle_rows
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
ORDER BY first_year ASC, span_years DESC, vehicle_rows DESC;
```

If you want “long time ago” to mean “produced before a cutoff year” (e.g., before 1970), tell me the year and I’ll add a filter and/or return only those makers.
I want to make sure we include car makers that had some production in the year 1970.

```sql
-- Makers that have at least one vehicle in 1970, with their overall time span in the data
SELECT
  cm.Maker,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
  (MAX(cd.Year) - MIN(cd.Year)) AS span_years,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_in_1970,
  COUNT(*) AS total_rows
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY first_year ASC, span_years DESC, total_rows DESC;
```
make sure to include the name of each matching car maker in the results.

```sql
SELECT
  cm.Maker AS maker_name,
  MIN(cd.Year) AS first_year,
  MAX(cd.Year) AS last_year,
  (MAX(cd.Year) - MIN(cd.Year)) AS span_years,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_in_1970,
  COUNT(*) AS total_rows
FROM car_makers cm
JOIN model_list ml ON ml.Maker = cm.Id
JOIN car_names  cn ON cn.Model = ml.Model
JOIN cars_data  cd ON cd.Id = cn.MakeId
GROUP BY cm.Id, cm.Maker
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN cd.Year = 1970 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY first_year ASC, span_years DESC, total_rows DESC;
```
